4.19.8.en: Instead of the covenant with You, O Life, I chose by my will to join the party of death, and darkness with corruption and injustice became my constitution.

4.19.9.en: * You came to me, and shared my nature.

4.19.10.en: I loved You, because You took the initiative of love toward me.

4.19.11.en: Let me possess You, O Immortal One.

4.19.12.en: I do not ask for long life, nor a multitude of offspring, nor memorials on earth.

4.19.13.en: For You are all my sufficiency and my satisfaction!

4.19.14.en: * I offer You my soul with all its energy, and my body with all its members and senses, that I may truly become a virgin.

4.19.15.en: Your Holy Spirit renews me and beautifies me, prepares me as a heavenly, immortal bride!

4.19.16.en: * You shine upon me with Your light, and You become my righteousness, and my holiness, and my salvation!

4.19.17.en: I desired to possess You with my whole being, so sin flees from my depths.

4.19.18.en: Dwell in me by Your grace, so that I know nothing but constant victory, with inner peace in the midst of the battle, and satisfaction in You.

4.19.19.en: * I become by Your grace a witness to the work of Your salvation, so that many may desire to possess You!

4.19.20.en: And many of the wicked return to You!

4.19.21.en: * My heart will not rest until You rest in mankind.

4.19.22.en: My soul grieves for those who set their hearts on their offspring.

4.19.23.en: And poured the spirit of evil into them, they became branches without a firm stem.

4.19.24.en: They became chaff scattered by the wind.

4.19.25.en: Instead of immortalizing the memory of their parents, they became grief and bitterness to them.

4.19.26.en: * I do not ask for a memorial in the world, nor do I desire long life here.

4.19.27.en: One day with You You count as a thousand years.

4.19.28.en: Your rich grace makes me a wonder!

4.19.29.en: Let death come, for it will not terrify me!

4.19.30.en: Behold, You prepare eternal rest for me!

4.19.31.en: * I do not ask for the outward dignity of old age, but I ask Your grace that gives wisdom.

4.19.32.en: By Your Holy Spirit You grant me the strength of youth, and by Him I enjoy the wisdom of the elders.

4.19.33.en: * I lift my eyes, and I see Your beloved Enoch with You, You translated him to You, because he cleaved to You.

4.19.34.en: You carried him from among the wicked, lest his soul be tormented by their iniquitous deeds, You snatched him from among his contemporaries, to keep him for a great work on the day of the coming of the Antichrist.

4.19.35.en: Your grace visited him that he might enjoy great glories!

4.19.36.en: * Finally what do I ask but to rest in Your bosom.

4.19.37.en: Keep me in You, You who took the initiative toward me with Your love.

5.0.0.en: 1 Then the righteous man shall stand with great boldness before the faces of those who afflicted him, and made his labours vain. 2 When they see him they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and be amazed at a salvation they did not expect, 3 and they shall say within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: "This is he whom we had sometime in derision, and a byword of reproach. 4 We fools counted his life madness, and his death dishonor. 5 How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot among the saints?! 6 We have erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined unto us, and the sun has not risen upon us. 7 We wearied ourselves in the paths of iniquity and destruction, and we wandered in wildernesses where there was no way, and the way of the Lord we have not known."

5.0.1.en: Then the righteous man shall stand with great boldness before the faces of those who afflicted him, and despised his labours. [1]

5.0.2.en: It is natural for the wicked to mock the righteous man, for it was said of Lot that "he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law" (Gen 19:14).

5.0.3.en: This chapter lifts the curtain on the righteous after their departure from this world. They stand in boldness before the wicked who afflicted them. The wicked had accused them of folly and ignorance, indeed madness, when they were giving their lives for the holy life in the Lord and the practice of sonship to God and their awaiting of eternal glory.

5.0.4.en: The wicked will discover that God does not forget a cup of cold water given by a righteous man out of his love for God, and that He will wipe away every tear from his eyes. And on the other side, they realize that God was very longsuffering toward them and that the cup of wrath has been filled against them.

5.0.5.en: What increases the bitterness of the wicked in the day of judgment is that they see the righteous - the object of their mockery and injustice - enjoying salvation and fellowship in the glories. They discover the error of their view of them as they realize the error of their view of the life and conduct of the wicked.

5.0.6.en: The wise man looks to the great day of the Lord, and sees the righteous man rising with great boldness as a son of God, awaiting the enjoyment of the fullness of glory. Those who afflicted him and made light of him and of the labors of his striving see him, and the situations are reversed as he comes to be in surpassing glory, and shame comes upon his opponents.

5.0.7.en: * Those who revile us do not know who we are, as we are citizens of heaven, and are enrolled in the city above, companions of the choirs of the Cherubim. Therefore let us not grieve, nor count their insulting us an insult, for if they had known us they would not have insulted us. Do they count us poor and despised? We do not count this an insult!

5.0.8.en: Tell me, if a traveler in the company of his servants went ahead of them and stayed in an inn for a short time waiting for them, and the innkeeper or some of the travelers behaved toward him rudely and cursed him, would he not laugh at their ignorance of him? Would not their error cause him gladness? Would he not feel a kind of contentment as though the insult were directed to another person than himself?

5.0.9.en: Let us behave thus. For we also are sitting in an inn awaiting our friends who are walking the same road, when we are all gathered together, then they will know who this was whom they cursed. These men will bow their heads and say: "Behold, he whom we, the foolish, mocked" (cf. Wis 5:3).

5.0.10.en: St. John Chrysostom What comforts the righteous here is that they share with the holy Righteous One who came unto His own, and His own received Him not (Jn 1:11). The Evangelist says of Him: "And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself" (Mk 3:21). As also the Apostle Paul shares, who says of himself and those with him who preach: "For whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God: or whether we be sober, it is for your cause" (2 Cor 5:13).

5.0.11.en: For on the great day of the Lord the Lord Christ comes as Judge, and those who made light of Him cannot look at Him. And so the prophets and Apostles and all the Church whom the wicked persecuted in the world stand to judge evil and the wicked. As the Lord Christ says: "And Jesus said to him, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel" (Mt 19:28). "That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel" (Lk 22:30).

5.0.12.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh has a strange portrayal of the Day of Judgment, and perhaps since he sees that the Lord is all love, therefore the wicked are not permitted to meet Him lest they ask His mercy, but they are permitted to see the glorified Apostles, which increases their bitterness, and the Apostles proceed to deliver the sentence upon the wicked.

5.0.13.en: * Fearful is the day on which the final judgment takes place, and on it the Son of God shines forth in great glory (Joel 2:1-11), on His right and on His left are lightnings of fire...

5.0.14.en: The throne of judgment is established in righteousness, and the Firstborn sits upon it in great glory to judge the peoples, and casts out in wrath and banishes in anger the accursed people who cried out in the court: Crucify him, crucify him (Mt 27:22-23); a veil of fire stands between Him and them lest they look at Him, lest mercies come upon them, and they do not let them look to the heights, lest they see His brightness and receive hope from Him; every man who deserves the sentence of death, if he saw the face of the King would not die; the peoples who loved Him and confessed His name enter into His own,...

5.0.15.en: Twelve thrones are prepared and the Apostles sit to judge the accursed people who did not believe in Him (Lk 22:28-30), and when they saw how much it had insulted Him and despised Him and abased Him because it denied Him, so that He did not make it worthy to enter the court like the peoples, the judgment of men is harsh upon men, therefore He delivered their judgment to men, because they deserve it so (2 Sam 24:14).

5.1.0.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh And when they see him they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and amazed at a salvation they did not expect. [2]

5.1.1.en: What increases the distress of the wicked is not only the torments prepared for them, but the glory enjoyed by the righteous, which was not in their imagination, for they are amazed at their salvation!

5.1.2.en: The wicked cannot look upon the Judge when they see His eyes a flame of fire, so they fear Him as Judge, telling the mountains to fall on them and the hills to cover them, for they have come to be in nakedness and shame as the first parents in Paradise were covering themselves with the leaves of trees. But whence will they get trees when they have been stripped of everything, even the mountains and hills have vanished. And what increases their bitterness is that He whom they see as a source of terror to them, behold, He embraces the righteous as the queen who rejoices in her heavenly King, who brings her into the bosom of the Father and she settles in it eternally.

5.1.3.en: As the righteousness of Christ shines and the fellowship of His features which the righteous have put on as a robe of glory for them, so in shame the wicked put on their evil deeds, especially their derision of the children of God, and their mockery of them, and they realize then that they have put on folly and vanity and corruption as garments that increase their nakedness and disgrace. Truly the glorified righteous will be separated from the perishing wicked eternally without partiality.

5.1.4.en: * As our Lord was teaching He said: from one house one shall be taken, and another left (Mt 24:40), if works do not draw a man to honor, the myriads of righteous who dwell with him do not profit him.

5.1.5.en: The righteous son does not benefit his father who sinned, and the sinful son does not take refuge in the righteous father.

5.1.6.en: The pure virgin does not save the mother who committed adultery, and the perfect brother does not benefit his lax brother.

5.1.7.en: From these things which our Lord taught, learn that one they take and the other they leave by discrimination (Mt 24:40).

5.1.8.en: Fear terrifies the two sisters in one house, and they cannot inquire together about the reason.

5.1.9.en: The height snatches that perfect one to fly in the air, and the deep draws the wicked one to be tormented in it.

5.1.10.en: The one is taken to meet the Bridegroom as it was said, and the other is left to return to the abyss as it is written (Mt 24:40).

5.1.11.en: The voice makes the daughter and her mother, who were at ease, tremble, and they fear and shake when they are separated to be transferred; brothers are separated like members from one another, and division is cast into their unity and scatters it.

5.1.12.en: Children are dropped and taken like bowels, and there is no room for the mother's womb to love them.

5.1.13.en: The love of women is cut off from their husbands, and the partner will not know his partner because of fear.

5.1.14.en: The wife is considered as a stranger by her husband, and though she was his own she is no longer his own because she was separated from him.

5.1.15.en: The married will not return to marriage, and fatherhood will not love its beloved.

5.1.16.en: And the love of brothers will not remain as it was because that equality is separated from mingling.

5.1.17.en: Fear cuts off the news between the two sisters, and that story which they were following will not end.

5.1.18.en: And if they were bound together at one mill, they will be separated from their unity as it is written (Mt 24:41).

5.1.19.en: And the word of love will not be completed between them, because terrifying fear nullifies their words.

5.1.20.en: It cuts off the beloved daughter's talk with her mother, and nullifies the speech of the doctors (teachers) and the researchers.

5.1.21.en: The pen breaks in the teacher's hand in an unusual way and nothing will be written with it forever, the boys leave the school where they were gathered, and will not come again another morning to learn.

5.1.22.en: Maxims fade and vanish from the wise, and no one will know anything but the fear of the resurrection.

5.1.23.en: Perplexity assails the philosophers in their thoughts, and they will remember nothing but to say only: Woe to us.

5.1.24.en: The story of theories and inquiries is cut off and nothing will be explained there except woe.

5.1.25.en: The word stumbles and falls from the tongue, and only the sound of wailing from Gehenna thunders.

5.1.26.en: No one will be consoled nor will his companion be consoled, for everyone will drink bitterness as he is tormented.

5.1.27.en: The young man will not support the old man while he suffers, and the father will not encourage his son lest he be depressed.

5.1.28.en: Each one is separated from his companion with great fear, and terror falls until one departs from his companion.

5.1.29.en: Behold, our Lord has spoken of the final judgment: they take the one and leave the other as we said (Mt 24:41).

5.2.0.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh And they will say to one another, repenting and sighing: [3]

5.2.1.en: The wicked repent of the conduct they followed in this world, but since the Day of Judgment has come, the opportunity to return to God has been lost to them.

5.2.2.en: * "For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?" (Ps 6:5). (The psalmist) also knows that now is the time to return to God, for when this life passes nothing remains but recompense according to our deserts... That rich man of whom the Lord speaks, who saw Lazarus at rest, lamented his state in the torments, and confessed in Hades, yes, and wished to warn his brothers that they might guard themselves against sin, because of the punishment that comes in Gehenna, which they do not believe in.

5.2.3.en: St. Augustine "Behold, he whom we sometimes made a laughingstock, and an object of derision.

5.3.0.en: We counted his life madness, and his end without honor. [4]

5.3.1.en: The wicked discover their folly, but after it is too late. They look to those whom they used to mock and count a laughingstock, whom they labeled mad, and they used to look to their end as dishonor without honor, and behold, they are in surpassing glories, enjoying what eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man (1 Cor 2:9).

5.4.0.en: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is with the saints? [5]

5.4.1.en: The wicked cannot see what the righteous see, nor hear what they hear, but what shatters them completely is that they have lost the opportunity to enjoy sonship to God and fellowship with the heavenly ones.

5.4.2.en: The author depicts how the salvation of the righteous becomes a punishment for those who wronged them and mocked them. The wicked are thunderstruck when they see the righteous, the object of their mockery, numbered among the glorified children of God, their portion with the holy heavenly orders. For the righteous come to be among them as though they were one of the heavenly orders. And this is the reward they receive, in which they become with them in the presence of God and fellowship with Him in the heavenly places.

5.4.3.en: The paradisal state which the true believer enjoys, according to St. Gregory of Nyssa, is a state of harmony and concord between him and the heavenly ones as they are God's creation full of love. [There was a time when the rational creation was one choir (chorus), turned toward the leader of the chorus, and moving in the direction of that overwhelming harmony that flows from the leader and from his commandment.]

5.4.4.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa also says that this harmony was at the level of the universe, between heaven and earth, where the first parents enjoyed the company of the angels; but they were corrupted by sin, and were driven out of this their society, and their descendants became as though in a strange world awaiting the moment in which they return to the enjoyment of union with the divine choir.

5.5.0.en: We are those who strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun did not rise upon us. [6]

5.5.1.en: The wicked confess their error, for eternal darkness has come upon them, because they rejected the Sun of righteousness, and did not let it rise upon them, so they became children of darkness. They lost the truth, and possessed falsehood.

5.5.2.en: Before the glory of the righteous the wicked stand in great remorse, because they left God the Truth, and rejected His love and salvation. All their possessions and pleasures were lost, indeed their life was lost, so they became in bitterness, but there is no longer a way to return to God.

5.5.3.en: St. Ambrose comments on the word "noon" in the statement: "And they made ready the present against Joseph came at noon" (Gen 43:25), showing that Joseph, as a type of the Lord Christ - the Sun of righteousness - at his coming the light of day comes as though it were noonday, and there is no place for darkness or night. He says: [The faith of Paul hastened to come at noon. Before, Paul was blind, and afterward he began to see the light of righteousness, for when one opens his way to the Lord and hopes in Him, the Lord brings his righteousness as light and his judgment as the noonday (cf. Ps 37:5-6). And when God appeared to Abraham at the oaks of Mamre it was at noon, and the eternal light of the presence of God shone upon him (Gen 18:1). It was noon when Joseph entered his house to eat. The day grows brighter when we celebrate the Holy Mysteries (where we partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord).]

5.5.4.en: * The spiritual sun shines only on the good and the holy, for we see in the Book of Wisdom the wicked weeping, saying: "the sun rose not upon us" (Wis 5:6), as the spiritual rain does not water the unrighteous, for he meant by the wicked that vineyard of which it was said: "I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it" (Isa 5:6).

5.5.5.en: St. Augustine * When the world was darkened by the darkness of the devil, and darkness came by sin which fell upon the world in the last stage, that is, when night came, this Sun was granted to rise by His birth.

5.5.6.en: First, before the appearance of the light, that is, before the rising of the Sun of righteousness, the divine inspiration was sent through the prophets like the dawn, as it was said: [I sent my prophets before the light] (cf. Jer 7:25). But afterward He sent His rays, that is, the splendor of His apostles, and shone upon the earth with the light of truth so that no one should stumble in the devil's darkness.

5.6.0.en: Maximus, Bishop of Turin We were satiated in the paths of iniquity and destruction, and passed through wildernesses with no roads, but the way of the Lord we did not know. [7]

5.6.1.en: The wicked think that evil is able to satisfy their needs, and do not realize that its end is utter destruction. As the Apostle says: "What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death" (Rom 6:21).

5.6.2.en: Did the path of iniquity and destruction satisfy them? He points here to the eternal path of thorns, for they become like those who are in the midst of countless thorns.

5.6.3.en: The wicked in the world were seeking satisfaction in the paths of iniquity and destruction, so they passed through barren wildernesses in which there was not the way that carries them to heaven; for they did not know the Lord as the Way.

5.6.4.en: He speaks of the ways of evil in the plural but the way of the Lord in the singular. For the demons offer many paths to bring man down to eternal destruction. But God offers us the Word of God and His wisdom our Lord Jesus as the only Way by which we go forth as on the wings of a dove to heaven.

5.6.5.en: * Isaiah says: "How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good" (Isa 52:7). He sees how beautiful and fitting is the proclamation of the Apostles who have walked with Him, who says "I am the way." And he praises the feet of those who walk in the rational way of Jesus Christ, and go through it to heaven. They proclaim good things, about the beautiful feet - that is, Jesus.

5.6.6.en: Origen * If the mere remembrance of your former state of slavery brings you shame, how much more is the shame of that very reality (slavery to iniquity).

5.6.7.en: St. John Chrysostom * The wicked will be punished; "the seed of the wicked shall be cut off" (Ps 37:28). As the seed of others will be blessed, so the seed of the wicked will be cut off, because the seed of the wicked are the works of the wicked... for they bear no fruit; their traces are for a short time; after this they seek them and find no reward for what they labored in.

5.6.8.en: St. Augustine * Death is in the company of the soul in the state of sin while it is in the body, and life is withdrawal from sin.

5.6.9.en: St. Clement of Alexandria St. Jude used in his epistle similar comparisons, regarding the passing life of the wicked. "These are rocks in your love feasts, feasting together without fear, shepherding themselves. Clouds without water, carried about by the winds, autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots. Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame, wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever" (Jude 12-13).

5.7.0.en: 8 What has pride profited us, and what good has our boasting of riches done us? 9 All that has passed away like a shadow and like a swift-running report, 10 or like a ship passing over the rippling water, which after its passing you cannot find its track, nor the line of its keel in the waves. 11 Or like a bird flying in the air; no sign of its passage is to be found. It strikes the light wind with its pinions, and cleaves the air with the force of its speed, and passes through with the beating of its wings, and afterward you find no sign of its passing. 12 Or like an arrow shot at a mark, so that the air is pierced by it, and at once returns to its state, so that the passage of the arrow is not known. 13 So also we, born and then vanished, had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness." 14 Thus did the sinners say in hell. 15 For the hope of the hypocrite is like chaff carried away by the wind, and like thin foam driven by the whirlwind, and like smoke scattered by the wind, and like the remembrance of a guest who lodged for a day and then departed.

5.7.2.en: And what good has the wealth we boasted of done us? [8]

5.7.3.en: The wicked discover the vanity of pride and arrogance, and also the vanity of wealth and riches which they used to count as the reserve of their honor.

5.7.4.en: Among all the ways and vices of the wicked, the wicked weep over their pride, which is the way of the devil who destroyed him and his angels. And also the love of wealth, for the love of money is the root of all evil (1 Tim 6:10). For pride drives the wicked to folly so that they exalt themselves even against God Himself, if not with the tongue then in the language of murmuring and rebellion and rejection of the divine commandment, and the love of wealth corrupts the heart so that love cannot reign over it, for its constitution becomes injustice and greed and hatred.

5.7.5.en: * It is pride that turns man away from wisdom, and folly became the fruit of turning away from wisdom.

5.7.6.en: St. Augustine The life of the wicked, empty of all virtue, is meaningless before God. Their life ends and their memory does not endure on earth or in heaven. Their life leaves no good trace after their death, indeed even the evil traces after the passing of some time are no longer remembered by many, but the virtues of the righteous or their love accompany them in heaven, for love never fails.

5.8.0.en: All that has passed away like a shadow, and like a report that passes quickly, [9]

5.8.1.en: Poor is the man who makes the shadow of a cloud a sign for his road, for the shadow soon passes, and the man loses his way. All the things of the present world and its lusts pass like a shadow, so they do not lift man's heart to God, the source of his life and eternal happiness.

5.8.2.en: Whoever is occupied with temporal honor and has all his thoughts absorbed in erecting memorials for himself is like one who walks after a false rumor, whose falsehood is soon exposed and that it has no true reality.

5.8.3.en: Poor is the wicked man who, instead of being joined to a cloud of witnesses (Heb 12:1), is occupied with its shadow. The Apostle Paul looked to this cloud not to occupy himself with its sight, but to join it, so as to become an inseparable part of the holy cloud that bears the Lord Christ.

5.8.4.en: The Lord appeared as a cloud to His ancient people to shade them from the heat and to lead them by day, longing that His people themselves become a shining cloud enjoying His presence and His manifestation above it, so that they become His throne.

5.8.5.en: Poor is the wicked man who, instead of seeking the divine truth so that he may enjoy the mysteries of God and experience the heavenly things, all that occupies him is that his life become a rumor that soon vanishes!

5.8.6.en: * "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Eph 4:26), and yet the sun has gone down many times. Leave your wrath too, since we now celebrate the days of the great Sun, this Sun of which the Holy Scripture says "unto you... the Sun of righteousness shall arise, and healing in its wings" (Mal 4:2). What does He mean by "in its wings"? That is, in His protection, for it is said in the Psalms: "hide me under the shadow of thy wings" (Ps 17:8). And as for those who repent on the Day of Judgment, but after the time has passed, who will grieve but without profit, it has already been prophesied in the Book of Wisdom what they will say when they repent and groan from anguish of spirit: "What hath pride profited us? or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow, we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun rose not upon us" (Wis 5:8-9, 6). That Sun rises on the righteous only, but as for this sun which we see daily, God makes his sun to rise on the evil and on the good" (Mt 5:45). The righteous ask to see that Sun while it dwells in our hearts by faith. So if you are angry do not let this Sun go down in your hearts upon your wrath, "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath," lest you become angry, and the Sun of righteousness go down from you and you remain in darkness.

5.9.0.en: St. Augustine Or like a ship passing over the waves of the water, which finds no trace of its passage, nor the line of its bottom in the waves. [10]

5.9.1.en: The third comparison the wise man gives us of the reality of the life of the wicked is the concern to look at the line that appears in the midst of the waves by the passing of a swift ship in the midst of the sea. For this line soon disappears and no trace of it remains on the moving waters. Poor is the man who, instead of entering the ship of Christ, that is His Church, to enjoy the riches of His gifts! stands a spectator outside and so does not enjoy eternal salvation.

5.9.2.en: The psalmist says of the life of the wicked: "like the dust which the wind driveth away from the face of the earth" (Ps 1:4). And of the righteous the Apostle says: "Consider the end of their conversation, and imitate their faith" (Heb 13:7).

5.9.3.en: Noah's ark as a ship is in truth a divine plan, in which God arranged the salvation of man, for God Himself shut the door of the ark and kept it until the end of the flood. So also the Church of the New Testament is a divine arrangement, for by divine grace we receive our membership in the Church, and the Holy Spirit closes our inner doors, so that the waters of evil do not seep into the ship of our life and it loses its balance. If the ship points to the Church as a refuge of salvation, then the wicked are not concerned to enter the Church as members in it, but are satisfied to look at it from afar to criticize it. They follow the line that appears in the midst of the waves by the Church's passing through the sea of this world, and so lose their salvation.

5.9.4.en: St. Augustine pointed to Noah's ark as a symbol of the Church, saying: [The ark is without doubt the symbol of the city of God in its pilgrimage through history.]

5.9.5.en: * The body of the Church as a whole is like a ship, carrying people of various races, in the midst of a violent storm...

5.9.6.en: God the "Father" is the owner of the ship.

5.9.8.en: The bishop is like the overseer, and the priests are the sailors, the deacons are the rowers, and the teachers of the catechumens are the attendants.

5.9.9.en: Homilies attributed to Clement * Whoever remains outside the Church is outside the camp of Christ.

5.9.10.en: * He is not a Christian who is not within the Church of Christ.

5.9.11.en: * For how can anyone be with Christ if he does not walk within the bride of Christ, and is not found in His Church?!

5.9.12.en: * Whoever does not have the Church as mother cannot have God as father!

5.9.13.en: St. Cyprian * The sea is the world, the Church went down into it to the depth but did not perish because its captain Christ is skilled.

5.9.14.en: Since it bears the cross of the Lord it bears the victory over death within it...

5.9.15.en: The sailors are the two Testaments (the Old and the New).

5.9.16.en: And the ropes surrounding it are the love of Christ which binds the Church.

5.9.17.en: The net that is with it is the font of the new birth which renews the believers.

5.9.18.en: The Holy Spirit dwells in it as a skilled sailor by whom the believers are sealed...

5.9.19.en: It has anchors of iron that hold it. They are the commandments of Christ Himself, strong as iron!

5.9.20.en: It has sailors on the right and left, servants like the holy angels who steer the Church and keep it.

5.9.21.en: The ladder by which we go up to the deck of the ship is the remembrance of the sufferings of Christ, by which the hearts of believers are lifted to heaven.

5.9.22.en: The sails raised above the ship are the fellowship of the prophets and martyrs and Apostles who enter into their rest.

5.9.23.en: Father Hippolytus * The sea cannot be crossed unless the sign of victory, that is the mast, remains on the ship without harm.

5.9.24.en: The Martyr Justin Or like a bird that flies in the air, so that you find no proof of its path.

5.10.0.en: It strikes the light wind with its wings, and cleaves it with a sharp whistling, and passes flapping its wings, and then you find no sign of its passing. [11]

5.10.1.en: Their memory on earth is like the trace of a ship cleaving the waters of the sea, appearing quickly and then disappearing. But in heaven there is no existence of the memory of the wicked because their life is like a bird that moves its wings to strike the air, but after its passing we find no trace in the air, nor does any line move to show its route; or like an arrow that passes through the air and leaves no line announcing its path.

5.10.2.en: The wicked man searches for the trace that a swift bird leaves in its flight, and behold, his life is lost behind a mirage that does not quench and traces that have no existence, instead of being occupied with looking at the line that the bird followed. It behooves the believer to become himself a bird that ascends by the Holy Spirit of God in the riches of divine grace from glory to glory (2 Cor 3:18), that perhaps he may attain the life of the stature of the fullness of the heavenly Christ (Eph 4:13).

5.10.3.en: * So, my brethren, is our existence, we who live in a temporary life. So is our recreation on earth. We came into being from nothing, and after existence, dissolution. We are illusory dreams... like the flight of a passing bird, and like a ship that leaves no trace of its path in the sea (Wis 5:10), a particle of dust, vapor, early dew, a flower that quickly appears and quickly dries. For man, his days are as grass, and as a flower of the field, so he flourishes.

5.11.0.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Or like an arrow shot at a mark, so that the air is pierced by it, and at once returns to its state, so that the passage of the arrow is not known. [12]

5.11.1.en: What is the arrow whose trace in the air the wicked are occupied in seeking when the archer shoots it toward the mark? I think it is the Lord Christ whom the Father directs to the hearts of believers, so each of them cries out with joy: "I am wounded with love" (Song 2:5)

5.11.2.en: * The bride praised the spear-thrower for his accurate aim, for he shot her with his arrow. So the bride said: "I am wounded with love" (Song 2:5). These words mean that the arrows of the Bridegroom have penetrated into her heart. The marksman of these arrows is Love (1 Jn 4:8), who sends "his chosen arrow" (Isa 49:2), the Only-Begotten Son, to those who are saved, and then dips the point of the threefold arrow into the spirit of life. And the point of the arrow is faith, and by it God presents the marksman and likewise the arrow together to the heart, as the Lord Christ says: "If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him" (Jn 14:23).

5.11.3.en: Therefore the soul that has been lifted to higher divine degrees sees within itself the arrow of sweet love which wounded it, and boasts of this wound, saying: "I am wounded with love." O beautiful wound, and sweet arrow, which brought life into my heart! For the penetration of the arrow has opened a door and an entrance for love, and it is the imaginary change from the shooting of arrows to the joy of the wedding.

5.11.4.en: We all know how the archer grasps the bow and his skilled hands work: the left hand holds the bow, while the right hand draws the flexible string, and so the arrow moves backward with its notched end. Then the left hand directs the arrow to the target. We mentioned before that the bride was the target, and now she sees herself as though she were the arrow in the hands of the owner of the bow. So He holds her with His right hand in one way, and in another way with His left hand...

5.11.5.en: God is the Bridegroom and the marksman, and He treats the pure soul as the bride, He aims His arrow at a good target. Therefore He allows His bride to share His incorruptible eternity, and bestows on her years and long life with His right hand. And gives her with His left hand the gift of His eternal life, and the greatness of God, in which those who seek greatness in the world do not share with Him. For this reason the bride says: "His left hand is under my head: (Song 2:6). For this is the way in which the arrow is aimed at its target. "And his right hand doth embrace me." As though the bride were saying that God's right hand receives me and draws me backward, in order to ease my journey upward where He directs me without my being separated from the hand of the bow-holder. And at the same time I shall be carried far away by His work in aiming, and I feel rest between the hands of the bow-holder: the Proverbs say of the qualities of these hands: "Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour" (Prov 3:16).

5.11.6.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa We can briefly compare the righteous and the wicked.

5.11.7.en: · The righteous longs to join the shining cloud of witnesses, and the wicked is occupied with the shadow of a cloud that soon disappears.

5.11.8.en: · The righteous wishes to record his name in the book of eternal life, and the life of the wicked becomes like a rumor that passes and has no existence or memory.

5.11.9.en: · The righteous delights to sail in the ship of Christ to enjoy salvation, and the wicked is content to look at the line that appears by its sailing for a time and then disappears.

5.11.10.en: · The righteous wishes to be like the eagle, soaring in the heavenly places, and the wicked searches for the trace of the eagle's flight and finds no existence for it.

5.11.11.en: · The righteous catches the stroke of the divine arrow, and his soul rejoices in the wounds of divine love, while the wicked is occupied with looking at the air, seeking the trace of the arrow's passage.

5.12.0.en: So we also, as soon as we were born began to vanish, and we had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness. [13]

5.12.1.en: The wise man portrays the life of man as, no sooner does it begin than the feeling of death accompanies it, so he awaits when death will come upon him, and vanishes from the world. Moreover, on the other side, since human nature has been corrupted, man finds no sign to lay hold of by which to show some virtue, but his constant feeling of weakness consumes his life.

5.12.2.en: The hope of the wicked is like chaff that the wind carries away, and like thin foam that the whirlwind drives.

5.13.0.en: It is scattered like smoke in the air, and passes away like the remembrance of a guest of one day. [14]

5.13.1.en: Since the wicked man puts his hope in the goods of the world and its pleasures and the lusts of the flesh, he soon loses his hope, for he counts it like chaff scattered by the raging wind, or like the foam that appears behind the speeding ship and the whirlwinds drive it away, or like smoke scattered in the air, or like the remembrance of a man whom he hosts for a day and does not return.

5.13.2.en: * Clouds without water, these in whom there is not the divine Word of the fruit-bearer. They are dead with double death: first, because they sinned in wickedness. Again that they are delivered up to the punishments God has prepared for them. A man can be said to be dead while alive, but he does not enjoy his inheritance.

5.14.0.en: 16 But the righteous shall live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord, and they have care from the Most High. 17 Therefore they shall receive a kingdom of honor, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord, for with His right hand He will cover them, and with His arm He will defend them. 18 He will take His zeal as armor and will arm the creation for vengeance on His enemies. 19 He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment as a helmet, 20 and will take holiness as an invincible shield, 21 and He will sharpen His wrath as a keen sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the foolish. 22 Then shall the thunderbolts of lightning go forth unerringly, and from the well-strung bow of the clouds they shall fly to the mark. 23 And His indignation shall stone them with great hail, and the waters of the seas shall rage against them, and the rivers shall meet with fierce violence. 24 And a mighty wind shall rise against them, a whirlwind shall scatter them, and iniquity shall lay waste all the earth, and ungodliness shall overturn the thrones of the mighty.

5.14.1.en: If the wicked have no lasting memory, the righteous live with the Lord Christ for ever, who pronounces them blessed, saying: "Blessed are those who mourn now, for they shall be comforted" (Mt 5:4). And the Apostle says: "let us run with patience the race that is set before us" (Heb 12:1), that we may enjoy the unutterable glories of heaven.

5.14.2.en: But the righteous shall live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord, and they have care from the Most High. [15]

5.14.3.en: The wise man tries to depict the blessed state that the righteous enjoy on the day of the Lord. Among what they enjoy:

5.14.4.en: A. Eternal life, "they shall live for ever"; what is this immortal life which death cannot approach, except Him who said: "I am the life." He who died once in the body by His will, since He said: "I have power to lay it down" (Jn 10:18). Death could not have approached Him if He had not delivered Himself up through His love for all mankind and His obedience to the Father, to enter - as St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian says - into the belly of death and burst it, and bring out those whom the devil had formerly captured in Hades.

5.14.5.en: We obtain it here on earth, so death does not approach our souls, and we meet Him face to face, and death can no longer touch our glorious bodies which are in the image of the body of our Lord who rose from the dead.

5.14.6.en: B. "Their reward is with the Lord"; the greatest thing the believer receives is that he finds his reward is the Lord Himself, who gives him of what He has, where he enjoys fellowship in heavenly glory.

5.14.7.en: C. Perhaps the realization of the crowned believer in heaven is that he discovers in new depths God's care, which not only does not stop in heaven, but those who enjoy heaven continue to perceive the warmth of the divine embrace, and remain for ever enjoying new mysteries that are revealed more and more!

5.15.0.en: Therefore they shall receive a glorious kingdom, and the crown of beauty from the Lord's hand, for with His right hand He will cover them, and with His arm He will defend them. [16]

5.15.1.en: The wise man continues his discourse on the blessed heavenly life, saying:

5.15.2.en: D. "They shall receive a glorious kingdom," where all become kings or queens, or all become the queen who sits at the right hand of the King (Ps 45:9). It is a glorious kingdom! The greatness of each man increases through the greatness of his brethren. For in the kingdoms of this world, when someone takes the seat of government his rivals grieve, and many envy him. But in heaven each man who enjoys this position does not have it alone, but realizes that the secret of his glory and honor and joy is that all the believers of the Old and New Testaments share this glory with him.

5.15.3.en: E. "The crown of beauty from the Lord's hand," it is the crown of true beauty, because it is from the Lord's hand, it bears the reflection of the glory and splendor of the Lord.

5.15.4.en: F. "For with His right hand He will cover them," as though the wise man sees the whole Church, having become the one queen bride, sitting at the right hand of the King, and as the reflection of the Bridegroom's splendor shines from them He embraces them, as one who covers them.

5.16.0.en: G. "With His arm He will defend them," from whom does He defend them? There is no longer any enemy to oppose, nor any sin to creep into the mind, so why does He defend them? The Church remains, enjoying heavenly peace and divine joy, praising the Lord who kept her in the wilderness of the world and brought her into the heavenly Canaan, and shut the door, so that she may remain with Him and in Him, kept by His surpassing love. 4. The Lord the Judge takes His zeal as complete armor, and arms the creation to repel His enemies. [17]

5.16.1.en: What is the zeal of this Righteous One but His surpassing love for His bride; this is the weapon with which He broke the devil and all the kingdom of darkness by His cross.

5.16.2.en: He arms His bride with the same weapon, which is the zeal of love, so that the devil - who knows not love but hatred and malice - finds nothing of his own in the heavenly bride.

5.16.3.en: St. Jacob of Serugh depicts for us a dreadful scene, which is that as soon as a soul departs from here the devil goes forth to it perhaps to find a place in it, and as he finds no place he is filled with rage and bitterness. For all that occupies him is that mankind share his eternal destruction.

5.17.0.en: He puts on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment as a helmet. [18]

5.17.1.en: After speaking of the righteous in the plural he now speaks of the Righteous One in the singular, as he fixes his gaze on the one Righteous, our Lord Jesus Christ, God incarnate, as He carried us in Himself to give us what is His, and to open for us the way of glory.

5.17.2.en: The Lord Christ comes on the day of the resurrection to reward the righteous and recompense the wicked with great zeal.

5.17.3.en: Also every believer who is united with the holy Righteous One bears His righteousness, and the Lord Christ becomes a shield for him, protecting him from the arrows of the enemy.

5.17.4.en: The only way to victory over the devil is union with God and cleaving to the truth and keeping His commandments, so the believer bears practical witness to the truth by his life.

5.17.5.en: There is no way to witness for the heavenly Holy One except that we bear the spirit of holiness and experience with the Apostle Paul the sitting in the heavenly places. For without holiness wrath comes upon us, or we drink of the cup which we fill for ourselves by our unholiness.

5.17.6.en: Nature itself does not bear the evil of man, so lightnings and clouds and torrents and hail all these join together against the land of mankind which corrupted nature and defiled the earth.
